applies_to: extension hosts whose remote authority matches seclab+*

verdicts.allow_with_constraint: forwarded only if every named argument constraint holds
verdicts.prompt: held, surfaced to the user as a tab-labelled scope-expansion prompt, then forwarded or rejected
verdicts.rewrite: forwarded, but the trusted side substitutes a tab-scoped value (sentinel credential, partitioned key)
verdicts.deny: rejected with an error the extension host sees as an unsupported operation

invariants.statement: No real secret may enter a tab, in any form, through any surface.
invariants.enforced_by: every entry below whose capability includes credential-access must have verdict deny or rewrite; never allow, allow_with_constraint or prompt

invariants.statement: Caller identity (tab, extension) is bound to the connection and is never read from call arguments.
invariants.enforced_by: entries flagged identity_from_argument must have verdict deny or rewrite

invariants.statement: Any surface with no explicit verdict is denied.
RPC policy is keyed on the createProxyIdentifier sid string, never the MainContext property name and never the numeric nid.
invariants.enforced_by: rpc entries are keyed by sid; the drift check rejects a key that is not a known sid

invariants.statement: A token minted for the tab reaches it only as a sentinel, bound to no more than its parent's bindings, or to the bindings of a derivation rule the controller declared for that exact route.
invariants.rationale: Agreed with the broker session and recorded in docs/adr/20261104-broker-output-is-data.md. Stated in the same words on both sides deliberately: a reader who sees the filter's sentinel and the broker's derived credential described differently would reasonably conclude they are two mechanisms that could diverge, when they are one rule enforced at two points.
invariants.enforced_by: on this side, $getSession and $getPassword carry credential-access impact and identity_from_argument, so the no-real-secret-in-tab and identity-never-from-arguments checks already force them to deny or rewrite. The derivation bound itself -- that a derived token inherits no more than its parent's bindings -- is enforced by CredentialStore.derive in the broker, not here.
invariants.checked_by: check_drift.py::check_invariants for the filter side. The broker side is checked by broker/tests/unit/test_core.py::test_derived_credential_is_never_wider_than_its_parent, with broker/tests/unit/test_core.py::test_derive_trusted_widens_only_to_the_rule_and_keeps_its_sentinel covering the declared-rule exception and broker/tests/unit/test_core.py::test_r7_derived_children_never_outlive_their_parent covering lifetime, including a parent re-imported with an equal value.
invariants.filter_side_note: The clause after 'or' is the broker's, not this table's. It was added for the Copilot token (secure-agentic D7) so a controller can declare a wider derivation for one exact route. No surface here uses it: $getSession and $getPassword return a tab-scoped sentinel bound to the parent's bindings and nothing else, so the stricter half of the sentence is what this filter enforces. The amended wording is recorded in full so a reader comparing the two components does not find two different rules and have to guess which is current. Credential lifetime and revocation are enforced only in the broker: this filter hands out a sentinel and never revisits it, so if a parent credential is withdrawn nothing here notices or tells a tab. Recorded so neither side assumes the other is handling it.

invariants.statement: No command whose id begins 'seclab.' is reachable from a sandboxed host.
invariants.enforced_by: a deny rule on the prefix, and -- because commands.exact is resolved before rules -- a check that no exact entry with that prefix carries a reachable verdict. The filter also refuses the prefix at run time before consulting its table, so the guarantee does not depend on the table staying correct.

invariants.statement: Every surface class carrying a deny verdict must name the code that refuses it, and that code must exist in the patch series.
invariants.enforced_by: policy.enforcement maps each key prefix to a patch and a symbol; the gate fails when a deny verdict has no entry, when the patch is absent from patches/series, or when the symbol is absent from the patch

invariants.statement: No command may be given a verdict other than deny until the deferred-laundering residual is fixed, except the residual's recorded leaf exceptions, each validated.
invariants.enforced_by: residuals['deferred-laundering'].fixed is false, so the gate refuses any cmd: verdict that is not deny unless the id is in leaf_exceptions and its entry is allow_with_constraint with leaf: true, leaf_evidence and a validator

invariants.statement: The filter's decision log may only be treated as trusted evidence while a tab can neither forge lines in it nor write the file.
invariants.enforced_by: every MainThreadLogger.* method is deny, so $log cannot append to an existing logger by URI; and MainThreadFileSystem.$writeFile is constrained to this tab's own vscode-remote://seclab+ authority, so the window logs directory is unreachable, with $mkdir, $copy and $rename denied so there is no create-then-rename route

$handleProgressChunk.capability: push a progress chunk into a chat session on the trusted side
$handleProgressChunk.rationale: Callable over RPC despite not appearing in MainThreadChatAgentsShape2, because the dispatcher resolves actor[methodName] without consulting the interface. Chat rendering is a trusted-side surface that can present attacker-chosen content as assistant output, so a sandboxed host does not get it in v0.

$handleAnchorResolve.capability: resolve an anchor in rendered chat output

$getPassword.capability: read a stored secret for an extension id the caller names
$getPassword.constraint: the storage key is partitioned by the tab bound to the connection: {seclabTab, extensionId, key} (patch 0032). extensionId remains a claim, but only within this tab's partition, where every extension shares the one extension host a rogue extension already controls; nothing outside the partition, including UI-side extensions' secrets and other tabs', is addressable
$getPassword.rationale: extensionId is an RPC argument, so a hostile host can name any extension, including vscode.github-authentication, and read its stored sessions. The stored value is also global across windows, so without partitioning one tab reads another tab's secrets. The partition makes the tab, not the claimed extension, the unit of isolation: the filter permits this rewrite only once patch 0032 has registered it, and the validator holds the arguments to an extension id and a bounded key.

$setPassword.capability: write a stored secret under an extension id the caller names
$setPassword.rationale: Poisoning: a tab can overwrite another extension's stored session, including an auth provider's.

$deletePassword.capability: delete a stored secret under a caller-named extension id
$deletePassword.rationale: Same spoofable identity; worst case is destroying another extension's credentials.

$getKeys.capability: enumerate every stored secret key for a caller-named extension id
$getKeys.constraint: same partition as $getPassword; only keys in this tab's partition are listed
$getKeys.rationale: Enumeration is strictly worse than a single read: it gives the attacker the key names to then fetch.

$initializeExtensionStorage.capability: read an extension's global (shared: true, profile-wide) or workspace state, by a caller-named id
$initializeExtensionStorage.constraint: the storage key is partitioned by the tab bound to the connection, seclab-tab:<tabId>/<id>, in both scopes; storage migration is skipped for tab hosts; the id must be an extension id (patch 0032)
$initializeExtensionStorage.rationale: Every activation awaits BOTH mementos (extHostExtensionService.ts L504-L517), so denying either scope stops every extension activating. Unpartitioned, the caller-named id is used verbatim as a storage KEY in the profile or workspace store, so a tab could read any key there, not only extension state: other tabs' state for the same extension, UI-side extensions' state (the Tab Manager keeps pending routes in globalState), and workbench keys. Migration copies state from a source id into the target, which would import unpartitioned state into the partition, so tab hosts skip it.

$setValue.capability: write an extension's global or workspace state, by a caller-named id
$setValue.constraint: same partition as $initializeExtensionStorage; the value must be a state object
$setValue.rationale: Unpartitioned, a write under any key of the profile or workspace store: poisoning another tab's state, a UI-side extension's (the Tab Manager's pending routes), or a workbench key. Every Memento.update reaches this.

$registerExtensionStorageKeysToSync.capability: mark an extension's state keys for Settings Sync
$registerExtensionStorageKeysToSync.rationale: Settings Sync would carry tab state off the box and into the user's other machines. Not on the activation path: setKeysForSync is void and the proxy call is not awaited, so a denial surfaces only as an unhandled rejection in the extension host.

$getSession.capability: obtain an authentication session, including its access token
$getSession.constraint: return a session whose accessToken is a tab-scoped sentinel; the broker swaps it on egress that matches the credential binding. The extensionId argument is replaced with the connection-bound identity before any consent or trustedExtensionAuthAccess decision. Shared rule with the broker, stated identically in both places so they read as one mechanism: a token minted for the tab reaches it only as a sentinel, bound to no more than its parent's bindings. Applied here and by CredentialStore.derive in the broker; see docs/adr/20261104-broker-output-is-data.md.
$getSession.rationale: Returns a real reusable token into the sandbox, which violates no-real-secret-in-tab. The extensionId argument also drives the consent decision, so a hostile host can impersonate an already-trusted extension to skip the prompt.

$startFileSearch.capability: search for files by name under a folder, with caller-chosen options
$startFileSearch.constraint: the folder (argument 0) is null or a canonical vscode-remote resource of this tab; every URI nested in options (extraFileResources, changedFileUris, excludePattern[].uri) is the same; expandPatterns is absent or false, and no includePattern or excludePattern segment is one QueryBuilder.parseSearchPaths would make a search root (absolute, ~, a drive, ./ or ../), so a pattern cannot choose the roots; options is a whitelist of known keys with bounded primitive values, so an option this validator does not know is refused
$startFileSearch.rationale: vscode.workspace.findFiles; the benign control's findFiles step and most real extensions need it. With a null folder the query covers the window's workspace folders, which in a tab window are the tab's own. The positional rule covers argument 0 but not options: IFileQueryBuilderOptions declares extraFileResources and changedFileUris as URI arrays and excludePattern entries carry a uri, revive(options) materialises them, and QueryBuilder puts them on the query where the search backend stats them, a host-path existence oracle with file: URIs.

$lookupAuthorization.capability: retrieve the host's configured proxy credentials
$lookupAuthorization.rationale: Hands host proxy credentials to the caller. There is no sentinel form that a tab needs, because the tab's only egress is its own broker.

$lookupKerberosAuthorization.capability: obtain a Kerberos ticket for a caller-chosen service principal
$lookupKerberosAuthorization.rationale: A Kerberos token for an attacker-chosen SPN is a reusable host credential.

$readText.rationale: The clipboard routinely holds tokens and passwords the user has just copied. A tab can poll it. There is no argument constraint that makes this safe, and a prompt on every read is unusable, so it is denied outright in v0.

$writeText.rationale: Write-only. The residual risk is clipboard poisoning leading to the user pasting attacker text into a host terminal; that is accepted in v0 and recorded as a residual risk.

$executeCommand.capability: run any command in the trusted-side registry, with caller-chosen arguments
$executeCommand.constraint: the id argument must resolve to an allow or prompt verdict in the commands table; arguments are additionally validated by the per-command argument validators
$executeCommand.rationale: The id comes from the caller and is not checked against the caller's location, so the whole registry is reachable. This is the single widest surface and the reason the commands table exists.

$registerCommand.capability: register a command id the trusted side will route back to this host
$registerCommand.constraint: the id is a command id, outside the fork's reserved prefixes, not one the trusted side owns (the workbench's ids from the inventory and the UI-side extensions' ids, SECLAB_TRUSTED_COMMAND_IDS), and not registered by anyone at the time of the call. The registration routes back only to this extension host: MainThreadCommands is per host and its handler calls this host's $executeContributedCommand
$registerCommand.rationale: The registry is last-writer-wins (CommandsRegistry.registerCommand unshifts), so without a collision check a tab can shadow a trusted command id and receive its invocations, with the arguments trusted callers pass, from the UI, another extension, or a command: link. Refusing ids the trusted side owns covers ids it registers lazily, after the tab connected; refusing any registered id covers the rest. Residual: the 172 command ids the inventory could not resolve statically are not in the trusted set, so a lazily registered one of those can be pre-empted until the trusted registration replaces it. Not on the activation path (ExtHostCommands.registerCommand does not await it), but every extension command invoked from a menu, keybinding or the palette needs it.

$unregisterCommand.constraint: only ids this tab registered (validator bookkeeping); upstream already confines it to this host's own registrations
$unregisterCommand.rationale: MainThreadCommands is instantiated per extension host and _commandRegistrations is its own DisposableMap, so deleteAndDispose can only reach a registration this host made; an id it never registered is a no-op. The validator keeps that true if upstream stops doing it structurally. Measured on an ordinary session as an extension's dispose path.

$getCommands.rationale: Returning the full registry tells an attacker exactly which host commands exist to try. The intended constraint, filtering the RESULT to the ids this tab may execute, is a response rewrite, which an argument validator cannot express; it was recorded as allow_with_constraint and enforced as a deny all along (constraint not implemented), so the verdict now says what happens (review round 10, finding 3). Not on any ordinary-session path (absent from the trace); an extension that calls vscode.commands.getCommands gets a rejection.

$ensureActivation.capability: activate the extensions that provide a file system scheme
$ensureActivation.constraint: the scheme is the tab's own file system: file (what a remote extension host sends for its own files) or vscode-remote; nothing else. Residual: file triggers onFileSystem:file activation in the trusted UI host (the event fires before the provider check); no UI-side extension declares it at a717861c or in this fork
$ensureActivation.rationale: workspace.fs on a scheme the extension host does not serve itself awaits this, so it gates every workspace.fs call (measured: 20 calls on an ordinary session). IFileService.activateProvider returns at once for a scheme that already has a provider; otherwise it fires onFileSystem:<scheme> activation in the trusted UI host as well as the tab's. Pinning it to vscode-remote leaves only the tab's own file system.

$readFile.capability: read any URI the IFileService can resolve
$readFile.constraint: the positional URI rule: every UriComponents argument revives, canonically, to vscode-remote://seclab+<this tab> or untitled:
$readFile.rationale: Any scheme is accepted, so file: and vscode-userdata: reach host files, including user settings which can hold tokens. The scheme and authority constraint is what removes the credential reach: a tab can only name paths inside its own sandbox.

$writeFile.capability: write any URI the IFileService can resolve
$writeFile.rationale: A host write is a code-execution primitive: shell rc files, LaunchAgents, git hooks outside the workspace.

$tryOpenDocument.capability: open a text model on a caller-named resource; the model is then synced to the extension host
$tryOpenDocument.constraint: argument 0 is a canonical vscode-remote resource of this tab (no other scheme, not untitled:); argument 1 is any plain object (openTextDocument(uri) sends the URI itself there) whose encoding, if present, is a short string, the only field the reachable branch reads
$tryOpenDocument.rationale: vscode.workspace.openTextDocument; the benign control's openTextDocument step and most extensions need it. The default branch hands the URI to ITextModelService.createModelReference, which reads the real bytes for any scheme the file service serves, and the model is then synchronised to the calling host: with file: or vscode-userdata: (user settings, which can hold tokens) that is a host read into the tab. untitled: is refused too, because its branch maps a path through toLocalResource and probes existence.

$tryShowTextDocument.capability: open an editor on a caller-named resource in this window
$tryShowTextDocument.constraint: argument 0 is a canonical vscode-remote resource of this tab; options has only position, preserveFocus, pinned and an integer selection
$tryShowTextDocument.rationale: vscode.window.showTextDocument. IEditorService.openEditor on an unconstrained URI opens a host file in the window, and an open model is synced to the tab, so it is a read primitive as well as UI; the URI rule removes the read. What remains is that a tab can choose the active editor in its own window, which is a nuisance, not a boundary crossing (patch 0012 keeps the window from taking focus from the user's other apps).

$unregister.capability: dispose a language feature registration by handle
$unregister.rationale: The handle is looked up in this MainThreadLanguageFeatures instance's own map, one instance per extension host, so a tab can only dispose registrations it made; unknown handles are a no-op. Every $register* in this service stays denied in this landing (a tab-provided item's command, command: links and remote images would reach trusted UI and the global ICommandService on a user gesture; deferred to a structural response-side control), so today this has nothing to dispose; it is allowed so that dispose paths do not raise errors.

$getInitialState.capability: read whether this window is focused and active
$getInitialState.rationale: Returns hostService.hasFocus and userActivityService.isActive for this window: no path, identity or host configuration. The same two facts are pushed to the extension host on every change ($onDidChangeWindowFocus/$onDidChangeWindowActive), so denying the initial read only leaves vscode.window.state wrong. Residual: a tab can time work for when the user is away, which it can do regardless. Measured on an ordinary session (ExtHostWindow's constructor).

$openUri.capability: hand a caller-chosen URI to the host OS opener
$openUri.constraint: the prompt names the tab and shows the full target; allowTunneling and allowContributedOpeners are forced to false
$openUri.rationale: openExternal is a silent exfiltration channel that bypasses the tab broker entirely, and on some platforms a URI is a code-execution primitive.

$asExternalUri.capability: resolve a URI to a host-reachable form, creating a tunnel if needed
$asExternalUri.constraint: tunnel creation is prompted and the resulting tunnel is bound to this tab
$asExternalUri.rationale: Resolving can mint a tunnel, which is a route out of the tab that the broker does not see.

$openTunnel.capability: forward a port between the host and the tab
$openTunnel.constraint: prompt naming the tab, the port and the direction; the tunnel is torn down with the tab
$openTunnel.rationale: A forwarded port is a route that bypasses the broker and can reach host-local services.

$setRemoteTunnelService.capability: point the tunnel service at a process id the caller chooses
$setRemoteTunnelService.rationale: A caller-chosen process id on the trusted side is not something a contained tab needs.

$tryStartChatRequest.capability: run a language-model chat request that the trusted side executes with the user's model credentials and quota
$tryStartChatRequest.rationale: The call is served on the trusted side: $tryStartChatRequest forwards to ILanguageModelsService.sendChatRequest in the workbench, so the model call, its credentials and its quota are the user's, not the tab's. Allowing it would give a tab a credentialed egress channel that does not pass through its broker, with the prompt as an unbounded exfiltration field. Denied in v0; if it is ever allowed it stays a trusted-side call (never a broker binding) and needs the prompt treated as data plus a per-tab rate limit.

$registerLanguageModelProvider.capability: register the tab as a language-model provider for the trusted side
$registerLanguageModelProvider.rationale: This is the dangerous direction, and it inverts the usual threat. A registered provider's sendChatRequest proxies $startChatRequest into the *registering* extension host, so a tab that registers a provider receives the trusted-side agent's full message array -- which may carry content the agent gathered from outside the tab -- and returns response parts the trusted agent consumes, including tool calls it will then execute with host privileges. The tab stops being a consumer of the model and becomes the model.

$onLMProviderChange.capability: signal a provider change for a vendor
$onLMProviderChange.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$unregisterProvider.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$reportResponsePart.capability: push a response part for a pending request
$reportResponsePart.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$reportResponseDone.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$selectChatModels.capability: enumerate the models available to the user
$selectChatModels.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$countTokens.capability: count tokens for a string or message
$countTokens.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$cancelLanguageModelChatRequest.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$fileIsIgnored.capability: ask whether a URI is ignored by content exclusion
$fileIsIgnored.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$registerFileIgnoreProvider.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$unregisterFileIgnoreProvider.rationale: Part of the language-model surface, which is denied wholesale in v0. These are the supporting methods for $tryStartChatRequest and $registerLanguageModelProvider and have no meaning without them.

$onUnexpectedError.capability: report an error into the window error handler
$onUnexpectedError.rationale: The extension host's own plumbing. Denying it does not contain a tab, it stops the tab working at all: measured on the first patched build, where the extension host never activated anything and the absent host marker read as containment (docs/edr/20261106-rpc-core-proof-run.md). The body deserialises the error and calls onUnexpectedError; it grants no capability and returns nothing. Denying it is self-amplifying by construction: the denial is itself an unexpected error, reported through the same denied channel. Measured at 92,365 calls in one window on a clean boot with no hostile extension installed. The payload is tab-chosen text and is treated as tab data by every consumer. Residual: a tab can make the host write to its own error log; that is bounded by the window log's own rotation, and the rpc-filter decision log aggregates repeats per key so it cannot be used to hide a denial.

$logExtensionHostMessage.capability: write the extension host console through the log service
$logExtensionHostMessage.rationale: The extension host's own plumbing. Denying it does not contain a tab, it stops the tab working at all: measured on the first patched build, where the extension host never activated anything and the absent host marker read as containment (docs/edr/20261106-rpc-core-proof-run.md). Routes a console entry to the log service, and to the local console only when the window was started with the development flags. No capability, no return value. The entry is tab-chosen text and is treated as tab data.

$onWillActivateExtension.capability: tell the window an extension is about to activate
$onWillActivateExtension.rationale: The extension host's own plumbing. Denying it does not contain a tab, it stops the tab working at all: measured on the first patched build, where the extension host never activated anything and the absent host marker read as containment (docs/edr/20261106-rpc-core-proof-run.md). One call into _internalExtensionService._onWillActivateExtension with an extension identifier. It is a notification, not a capability, and it is on the path of EVERY activation, so denying it is what stops any extension running in a tab at all.

$onDidActivateExtension.capability: tell the window an extension finished activating, with its timings
$onDidActivateExtension.rationale: The extension host's own plumbing. Denying it does not contain a tab, it stops the tab working at all: measured on the first patched build, where the extension host never activated anything and the absent host marker read as containment (docs/edr/20261106-rpc-core-proof-run.md). The same shape as $onWillActivateExtension plus three numeric timings and an activation reason. Forwarded to the internal service; grants nothing and returns nothing.

$onExtensionRuntimeError.rationale: The extension host's own plumbing. Denying it does not contain a tab, it stops the tab working at all: measured on the first patched build, where the extension host never activated anything and the absent host marker read as containment (docs/edr/20261106-rpc-core-proof-run.md). Deserialises the error, notifies the internal service and console.errors the message and stack. No prompt, no install path, no return value. Tab-chosen text, treated as tab data.

$setPerformanceMarks.rationale: The extension host's own plumbing. Denying it does not contain a tab, it stops the tab working at all: measured on the first patched build, where the extension host never activated anything and the absent host marker read as containment (docs/edr/20261106-rpc-core-proof-run.md). Hands marks to the timer service, bucketed by extension host kind; a tab is always remoteExtHost, so a tab cannot write marks attributed to the local host. Data only.

$onExtensionActivationError.capability: report an activation failure, with an optional missing dependency
$onExtensionActivationError.constraint: missingExtensionDependency (argument 2) is null or undefined; argument 0 is an extension identifier object and argument 1 a serialized error
$onExtensionActivationError.rationale: With a truthy missingExtensionDependency it reaches _handleMissingNotInstalledDependency, which prompts the user to INSTALL an extension the tab named, and _handleMissingInstalledDependency, which offers to reload or enable one. The validator admits only the null case, which notifies the internal service (the running-extensions view and an activation-error telemetry event) and console.errors the message; the development-window notification depends on trusted environment flags our builds do not set. Denying it entirely left an activation failure in a tab undiagnosable.

commands.note: Resolution is ordered: exact id first, then rules in order, then default_verdict. Categories are a GROUPING HINT and may only carry the verdict 'deny'. A command becomes reachable only through an explicit entry in 'exact', individually reviewed against its implementation. This is deliberate: the category is a substring heuristic over the command id, and the 2026-11-04 design review demonstrated it mis-grouped host-authority commands as editor-local (e.g. editor.action.accessibilityHelpOpenHelpLink opens an external link, and _workbench.editor.configureDefaultEditor matched 'editor.' before the underscore rule). A heuristic may withhold authority; it may not grant it.
commands.reachable_allowlist_status: Built from measured need: the ordinary-session trace (rpc-filter/probes/traces/20261106-ordinary-session.json) showed which commands every extension calls; each reachable id is reviewed against its implementation, carries an argument validator and a probe, and while the deferred-laundering residual is open must be one of its recorded leaf_exceptions. Nothing is allowed because it looked harmless in bulk.

_remoteCLI.openExternal.capability: open a caller-chosen URI externally, with tunnelling allowed
_remoteCLI.openExternal.rationale: Reachable both from $executeCommand and from the remote terminal channel's onExecuteCommand allowlist. It passes allowTunneling: true, so it both exfiltrates and can mint a tunnel.

_remoteCLI.windowOpen.capability: open a window on a caller-chosen folder or file
_remoteCLI.windowOpen.rationale: Opening a host folder in a new window starts an extension host over it, outside this tab's mount.

_remoteCLI.manageExtensions.rationale: Installing an extension is arbitrary code execution with whatever kind that extension declares.

_remoteCLI.getSystemStatus.rationale: Host inventory, process and path disclosure.

workbench.action.terminal.newLocal.capability: create a terminal on the host rather than in the tab
workbench.action.terminal.newLocal.rationale: In a remote window this explicitly creates a local, host-side terminal. Combined with sendSequence it is a direct host code-execution chain.

workbench.action.terminal.sendSequence.capability: write arbitrary bytes into the active terminal
workbench.action.terminal.sendSequence.rationale: Types into whichever terminal is active, which may be a host terminal. This is the second half of the newLocal chain and is dangerous on its own.

_setContext.capability: set a context key in the window's global context (vscode.commands.executeCommand('setContext', ...))
_setContext.constraint: the key is not declared by the workbench (RawContextKey.all()), not under seclab. / seclab: / config., matches a plain key shape of at most 256 characters, and has no value that this tab did not set; the value is a primitive, a URI, or a flat list or map of them, bounded in size
_setContext.rationale: Measured: 129 calls on an ordinary session (rpc-filter/probes/traces/20261106-ordinary-session.json), from every built-in that has menus or keybindings; denied, every extension's when-clauses stay false. The handler writes the window's global context with any key, so a tab could flip core or Tab Manager when-clauses and surface trusted menus and keybindings for host actions the user then triggers. Leaf: the handler only calls IContextKeyService.createKey, so nothing it does can reach ICommandService and launder. Residual: a hidden RawContextKey (declared with hide: true, absent from all()) or a dynamically built key the trusted side has not yet written can still be set first by a tab.

_executeHoverProvider.capability: run every registered hover provider (the tab's and UI-side ones) on a model the caller names
_executeHoverProvider.constraint: argument 0 is a marshalled URI that revives, canonically, to vscode-remote://seclab+<this tab> (no other scheme, not untitled:); argument 1 is a position
_executeHoverProvider.rationale: What vscode.executeHoverProvider calls; the benign control's hover step and any extension composing hovers need it. registerModelAndPositionCommand hands the caller's URI to ITextModelService.createModelReference, and in a remote window file: is the HOST disk, so an unconstrained URI reads host files back through UI-side hover providers. The URI rule keeps it to this tab's own resources, and rejects a URI whose cached string or fsPath disagrees with its components. Leaf: the handler resolves a model and calls providers; it does not reach ICommandService.

_executeCompletionItemProvider.capability: run every registered completion provider (the tab's and UI-side ones, including word-based completion) on a model the caller names
_executeCompletionItemProvider.constraint: argument 0 is a marshalled URI that revives, canonically, to vscode-remote://seclab+<this tab> (no other scheme, not untitled:); argument 1 is a position; argument 2 at most a short trigger string; argument 3 an item count of at most 1000
_executeCompletionItemProvider.rationale: What vscode.executeCompletionItemProvider calls. The handler calls ITextModelService.createModelReference(uri) on the caller's URI; with file: that is a host file, whose words come back through word-based completion. Same URI rule as _executeHoverProvider. Leaf: it resolves a model, calls providers and resolves items; a returned item's command is data for the caller, not executed here.

trusted_registration_ids.note: Command ids registered by trusted UI-side extensions in a tab window, which a tab may not register (validator tabCommandRegistration). The workbench's own ids come from the inventory (registered only under src/). The Tab Manager's ids are all under the reserved seclab. prefix. These are the built-in extensions whose manifest makes them UI-side (extensionKind starts with ui): their contributed commands, plus ids they register in code without contributing them, found by reading their sources at a717861c (simpleBrowser.api.open, vscode-testresolver.newWindowWithError). Hand-checked, not generated: a UI-side extension added upstream must be re-read (review round 10 finding 4; a scanner for extensions' registerCommand calls is the follow-up).

rules.rationale: The fork's own commands, which exist to let the *user* approve things the tab cannot do for itself. seclab.reviewChanges and seclab.confirmDeletes open modal approval dialogs in the Tab Manager. A tab that can raise those at will gets an unlimited supply of genuine-looking approval prompts; the click is still the user's, but the prompt is the attacker's, and a user who is asked often enough eventually says yes. The same reasoning covers the observability path: if a decision report were reachable as a command, a tab could forge events the UI labels 'trusted'. First rule in the list so the grouping is unambiguous, and backed by an invariant because a prefix rule alone would be overridden by an entry in commands.exact.
Terminals, tasks and debug sessions must start inside the tab. A host-side one defeats the whole containment.
Installing, enabling or updating an extension from inside a tab is arbitrary code execution and can escalate kind to ui.
Reveal-in-OS, open-folder and friends act on host paths outside the tab mount.
Opening or replacing windows moves work outside this tab's sandbox.
Settings are a code-execution vector through interpreter and tool path settings, and they persist beyond the tab.

Legitimately used by extensions to open docs and auth pages, and also an egress path around the broker. It is denied in bulk; individual ids are promoted to prompt in 'exact' once reviewed, because the category match is too coarse to tell vscode.open of a workspace file from one of an arbitrary external URI.
Port forwarding is a normal remote-development need and a route around the broker. Promoted to prompt per id in 'exact' once reviewed.
Underscore-prefixed ids are internal plumbing with no API contract and no argument validation expectations.

Mostly cursor, selection and navigation inside documents this tab already owns, but the category is a substring match on the id and demonstrably captures commands with host authority. Denied in bulk; the genuinely local ones are promoted individually in 'exact'.
Default-deny. An unclassified command is denied until someone classifies it.

channels.note: Channels the workbench registers on the remote connection. The REH server runs inside the tab and calls these directly; they never pass through RPCProtocol, so the MainThread* filter does not see them.

download.capability: the server names both the source and the destination URI of a download performed by the trusted side
download.rationale: DownloadServiceChannel revives both URIs from server-supplied arguments. The trusted side will fetch a URL the tab chooses, bypassing the broker, and write it to a host path the tab chooses. Our REH is launched over exec stdio and never needs the client to download for it.

mcpGatewayToolBroker.capability: the server lists and invokes MCP tools and reads MCP resources registered on the trusted side
mcpGatewayToolBroker.rationale: callToolForServer invokes a tool hosted on the trusted side with arguments the tab chooses. Host-side MCP servers run as host processes with host credentials, so this is a direct confused-deputy path to host code execution. readResourceForServer is a host read. Not covered by the forwarded review; found by the inventory scan.

tab_data.note: Values that originate in a tab and are interpreted with authority by the trusted side. Verdicts here are implemented by the named mechanism rather than by the RPC choke point.

command-uri-in-markdown.mechanism: markdown and hover strings that arrived from a sandboxed host are forced isTrusted=false, so embedded command: links do not execute

webview-content.mechanism: webview sessions for a sandboxed tab are routed through that tab's broker and given a CSP whose connect-src, img-src and script-src resolve only through it
webview-content.rationale: Webviews render in the local trusted renderer, so by default they have the host's network position and bypass the broker entirely.

terminal-osc-sequence.mechanism: shell-integration OSC sequences from a tab may not set trusted-side state such as the cwd used by host openers

workspace-configuration.mechanism: configuration delivered to a sandboxed host is filtered to workspace scope; machine and application scoped values, http.proxy userinfo, http.proxyAuthorization and extension token settings are withheld
workspace-configuration.rationale: IConfigurationInitData is sent to the host at startup and user-scope settings can carry secrets.

quick-input-password.mechanism: the trusted side keeps the typed value, registers it with the broker as a user-supplied credential, and returns a tab-scoped sentinel to the extension
quick-input-password.rationale: Required by no-real-secret-in-tab: a password box is a direct way to put a real secret into a tab.

uri-handler.mechanism: vscode:// callbacks destined for a sandboxed extension are shown to the user and stripped of credential-bearing parameters unless bound by the broker
uri-handler.rationale: OAuth redirect callbacks carry codes and tokens.

mcp-server-definition.mechanism: secret inputs and env values in MCP server definitions are replaced with tab-scoped sentinels before the server is launched in the tab

trusted_ai.note: Surface (e). Not reachable through the RPC filter: the chat agent runs in the trusted workbench, so when it reads a tab's files and invokes a trusted-side tool, no RPC crosses the sandbox boundary. The enforcement point is a separate patch that refuses the built-in chat and agent tools in a window whose remote authority is seclab+*, in code, so no user, workspace or remote setting can re-enable them. Entries here exist so the drift gate pins the surface: a new tool, or a setting whose scope becomes workspace-writable, has to be looked at.
trusted_ai.decision: v0 disables VS Code's built-in chat and agent tools in sandboxed windows. The measured reason, not a precaution: of 54 tool definitions upstream at this SHA, not one statically declares runsInWorkspace: true, so an 'allow only tools that run in the workspace' policy would have an empty allow set. There is no safe subset to keep in v0. Moving chat into the tab is the real answer and is planned separately (docs/plans/chat-in-tabs.md).
trusted_ai.why_the_filter_cannot_help: The tab's contribution is data, not a call. .github/copilot-instructions.md and .github/instructions/ are located in workspace root folders and auto-attached when applyTo is '**', and the generated system prompt instructs the model to follow them. The tab writes a file; the trusted-side agent obeys it; the host effect follows from a tool the agent chose. No RPC method was invoked by the tab at any point.

pushes.note: Server-initiated pushes: events the REH server sends to the trusted workbench, which the workbench then acts on. Generated by seclab_inventory/pushes.py from every IChannel.listen reachable from a channel taken off the remote connection. This is the opposite direction from the MainThread* RPC surface and is invisible to a filter that only watches calls the extension host makes. Unlisted keys take the table's default verdict, which is deny.

enforcement.note: Where each surface class is actually refused, and the patch that ships it. A verdict is a claim about runtime behaviour, and a claim with no named code behind it is decoration. check_drift.py::check_enforcement requires every key prefix carrying a deny verdict to appear here, requires the patch to exist in patches/series, and requires the named symbol to be present in it. The gap this closes was real: remoteTerminal.onExecuteCommand was documented as denied, exempted from the digest by a name-based skip, and enforced nowhere.

rpc:.mechanism: the RPC choke point, keyed on (proxy id, method) for seclab+ hosts

cmd:.mechanism: the command validator and taint, refusing tab-originated commands

chan:.mechanism: the channel guard on channels the client serves to the server

push:.mechanism: NOT a whole-class control. Each denied push is refused by not registering its own subscription, so every denied push key needs its own entry below. The prefix entry exists only to say so.

data:.mechanism: tab-supplied data is constrained at its sink, chiefly the URI authority check

ai-tool:.mechanism: built-in chat and agent tools are disabled in seclab+ windows

ai-setting:.mechanism: built-in chat and agent tools are refused in seclab+ windows, so a tab-written agent setting has no agent in that window to steer. The settings are additionally pinned to fixed values by patch 0017 on the agent-host branch; that is defence in depth, and naming it here would credit this branch with enforcement it does not ship.

residuals.note: Known gaps that the design does not close, recorded as data so a gate can hold the conditions they depend on. A residual written only in prose is forgotten exactly when it stops being true.

deferred-laundering.statement: A tab-originated command handler that DEFERS a global ICommandService call -- setTimeout, an unawaited promise, an event subscription -- escapes both the taint and the in-flight backstop.
deferred-laundering.why: The origin is threaded by rebinding ICommandService for the handler, and the backstop covers handlers that reach a global service instead. Both are scoped to the synchronous and awaited call tree: seclabInFlight is incremented at seclabExecuteFromTab and unwound when that promise settles. Work deferred past that point runs with no origin and a zero counter.
deferred-laundering.candidate_fix: Carry the origin in the invoker's disposable scope rather than a window-wide counter, so it follows the handler's lifetime instead of the call's duration.
deferred-laundering.safe_while: no reachable command can launder: every command is deny except the recorded leaf_exceptions, whose handlers are shown (leaf_evidence) never to reach ICommandService, so a laundered call has nothing to launder through
deferred-laundering.leaf_exceptions_why: The ordinary-session trace (rpc-filter/probes/traces/20261106-ordinary-session.json) shows every extension needs these three; the user approved them as the only leaf exceptions while the residual stays open, each with an argument validator because a leaf can still leak or spoof host state. Fixing the residual properly (candidate_fix) is a follow-up after this landing.
deferred-laundering.gate: check_drift.py::check_residuals fails if any cmd: surface is given a verdict other than deny while fixed is false, unless it is a recorded leaf exception whose entry is allow_with_constraint with leaf: true, leaf_evidence and a validator; and fails on a leaf exception that is not reachable
